classification.difficultyReason: Account for both possible first colours without replacement, update the second-draw probability in each case, and add the two weighted paths.

content.prompt: A bag contains two red jellybeans and two blue jellybeans.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A jellybean is drawn at random, its colour is recorded and it is returned to the bag. A second jellybean is then drawn. What is the probability that the second jellybean is red?

answer.worked:
After replacement, two of the four jellybeans in the bag are red.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{second red}) &= \frac24 \\ P(\text{second red}) &= \frac12\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A jellybean is drawn at random, its colour is recorded and it is then eaten. A second jellybean is drawn. What is the probability that the second jellybean is red?

answer.short:
$\frac12$

The second jellybean can be red after either colour is drawn first.
answer.worked:
If the first jellybean is red, one of the three remaining jellybeans is red. If the first is blue, two of the three remaining jellybeans are red. The two first-draw colours are equally likely, so add the probabilities of the two paths.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{second red}) &= \frac24\times\frac13+\frac24\times\frac23 \\ P(\text{second red}) &= \frac16+\frac13 \\ P(\text{second red}) &= \frac12\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Which part, (a) or (b), describes independent draws, and which describes dependent draws?

answer.worked: In (a), replacement keeps the chance of red on the second draw at $\frac12$ for either first colour. In (b), the chance of red on the second draw is $\frac13$ after red and $\frac23$ after blue, so it depends on the first colour.
